# Implementation Plan: Single-user PUBLIC happy-server on evyatar.dev (D-001 + mandatory edge)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"remote-connectivity-single-user-public-evyatar-server"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-29. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview
Expose the operator's single embedded per-daemon happy-server PUBLICLY at `https://happy.evyatar.dev` through an **outbound-only Cloudflare named tunnel**, so a codexu operator whose corporate policy blocks Microsoft Dev Tunnels can reach their own machine's Happy session plane from anywhere. Operator-approved supersession: for this task only, the fork-level `AGENTS.md` "never happy.evyatar.dev / never Cloudflare provider-swap" guardrail is superseded because this is the operator's own embedded per-daemon single-tenant server, not a central happy-server, and Cloudflare is mandatory edge defense after the new app-layer verifier, not the boundary by itself. Today the *entire* boundary is the Dev Tunnels gateway: `authenticateTunnel` is a no-op, `/pair/complete` returns key material to any caller, and the socket handshake is fail-open in tunnel mode. Public exposure is therefore **a from-scratch application-layer auth-plane build**, not a transport swap. We build a fail-closed Ed25519 paired-device verifier covering every tunnel-only HTTP route, the Socket.IO handshake (websocket + polling), and `/pair/complete`; layer a **mandatory** Cloudflare Access service-token edge (`CF-Access-Client-Id` + `CF-Access-Client-Secret`) as defense-in-depth; and make the BOOX enrollment path explicit: a public pairing invite carries/imports the evyatar.dev URL, short-lived pair secret, and per-machine Access service-token credentials before first contact, then the app persists those credentials and sends them on `/pair/complete`, HTTP, and Socket.IO. Single-tenant, opt-in, default-off behind a codex `Feature`; Dev Tunnels path unchanged.

### Technical Constraints
- happy-app has NO `@noble/*`/`tweetnacl`; mobile device-proof needs an RN-compatible Ed25519 (likely `react-native-quick-crypto`/`@noble` polyfilled). Codex same-machine attach must stay loopback. Build order: happy-wire shared signed-request schema + nonce/body-hash vectors → happy-server → app/cli/codex. 4-space tabs, `.spec.ts` tests, `privacy-kit` base64.
- Cloudflare edge auth is Cloudflare Access service tokens, not mTLS for this task: the app already centralizes custom headers through `tunnelFetch()`/`getMachineAuthHeaders()` and `buildTunnelSocketOptions()`, while there is no existing RN certificate storage or client-cert presentation path. App proof work must add per-machine `cloudflareAccessClientId` + `cloudflareAccessClientSecret` storage fields, keep them through `AUTH_CREDENTIALS_KEYS` normalization, and present them as `CF-Access-Client-Id` / `CF-Access-Client-Secret` on HTTP plus Socket.IO websocket and polling headers. Existing public-server validation in `app/(app)/server.tsx` uses an unauthenticated `fetch()`, and current pairing in `auth/pairing.ts` only knows Dev Tunnels connect tokens, so public mode also needs a first-contact enrollment flow that imports or manually enters the Access service-token credentials before `/pair/complete`.

## Approach
### Architecture
A new `auth: "public"` server mode permits a non-loopback bind ONLY when a fail-closed verifier + configured edge-auth expectation are present. A new `remoteDeviceAuth.ts` (modeled on `loopbackCapability.ts`) verifies an Ed25519 signature over a server nonce + method/path/body-hash from an already-paired device; the canonical signed-request envelope schema, nonce/body-hash canonicalization, and fixtures live in `@slopus/happy-wire` and are imported by server/app/cli plus consumed by codex tests instead of being duplicated. One shared helper feeds a single global public-mode HTTP hook AND the socket middleware (ws + polling). Do not secure public mode by piecemeal `app.authenticate` preHandlers: `configureApi()` installs a fail-closed hook before public routes are registered, and every method/path is denied unless it appears in an explicit allowlist with a named policy. That allowlist must cover `/health`, `versionRoutes`, `devRoutes`, both pair endpoints, `/files/*`, and the existing tunnel route set; `/pair/complete` is the only pre-enrollment policy and still requires the QR secret + operator-opened pairing window + replay-protected nonce, while `/pair/connect`, `/health`, version/dev routes, `/files/*`, and post-pair API routes require the device verifier or are disabled in public mode. A mandatory Cloudflare Access service-token edge fronts it for day-one fail-closed coverage; mTLS is explicitly out of scope until the app has native client-certificate storage/presentation plumbing. Edge setup creates a single-user Access application for `happy.evyatar.dev` with a service-token policy, records the expected token audience/policy in daemon config, and rejects every missing or incorrect `CF-Access-Client-Id`/`CF-Access-Client-Secret` request before the app-layer verifier runs. Public enrollment is explicit: the daemon/CLI opens a short-lived public pairing window and emits a one-time pairing payload containing the public URL, machine id, pair secret, and Cloudflare Access service-token credentials (with a manual-entry fallback for BOOX); the app imports or enters that payload, validates the server with those Access headers, calls `/pair/complete` with Access headers plus the pair secret and its public device key, then stores the returned machine data with `cloudflareAccessClientId`, `cloudflareAccessClientSecret`, and its device proof keypair. The BOOX app sends the Access service token from `getMachineAuthHeaders()` for HTTP and includes the same headers in Socket.IO `extraHeaders` plus `transportOptions.websocket.extraHeaders` and `transportOptions.polling.extraHeaders`. Verifier ships and passes the decisive acceptance test BEFORE the Cloudflare provider/public bind lands.
### Implementation Strategy
Preflight docs/scope guardrail (`AGENTS.md` + `docs/fork-notes.md` supersession, no code exposure) → server auth plane (verifier + pairing-window + gate tighten) → decisive acceptance test → cli provider + listener selection + public pairing invite contract → app Access service-token storage/header plumbing + public enrollment + device proof → codex gate → edge ops → docs. Server stories must be merged before exposure stories.

## Scope
### In Scope
- Shared `@slopus/happy-wire` signed-request envelope schema/test vectors; `auth:"public"` mode + global fail-closed HTTP auth hook with explicit method/path policy allowlist; Ed25519 device verifier over all tunnel routes including `/health`, versionRoutes, devRoutes, `/pair/connect`, `/files/*` local-storage fetches, and socket (ws+polling); `/pair/complete` window+QR gate; gate tighten; CloudflareTunnelDaemonProvider; Cloudflare Access service-token policy/config, public pairing invite/manual-entry flow, app service-token storage/header presentation in HTTP and Socket.IO, app proof attach + polling; codex Feature/remote-on; mandatory edge; docs.
### Out of Scope
- Default Dev Tunnels/loopback behavior; codex loopback attach; multi-tenant server; D-004 relay; LAN as primary; per-IP limit as enrollment defense; Cloudflare mTLS/client-certificate provisioning.

## Risk Areas
- ANY uncovered route/transport = open door (worse than today). RN crypto feasibility. e-ink pairing-window UX/clock skew. Vendor block. Single all-powerful key/revocation. Windows LocalSystem `.cloudflared` cred path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `@slopus/happy-wire` exports the public signed-request schema and deterministic nonce/body-hash/signature vectors, and server/app/cli/codex tests consume those vectors. Hostile internet client fail-closed on `/health`, `/v1/version`, any enabled dev route, `/pair/complete` (401, NO key material), `/pair/connect` (401, NO key material), `/files/*` when local storage is enabled, every tunnel-only route, AND socket handshake (ws+polling). Public-mode tests enumerate the global hook allowlist so any newly registered public route without an explicit policy fails closed; the decisive server test must derive the route inventory from the registered Fastify app (not a hand-maintained list) and assert every non-allowlisted route returns 401 with no key material or secrets in the response body. `assertOperatorIdentityGate` still throws on bare public bind w/o verifier+edge. Cloudflare Access is configured as a service-token Access application for `happy.evyatar.dev`; missing/incorrect `CF-Access-Client-Id` or `CF-Access-Client-Secret` are rejected for HTTP and WS upgrade, and valid headers reach the app-layer verifier. The CLI/daemon exposes a short-lived public pairing invite/manual-entry payload containing the evyatar.dev URL, pair secret, machine id, and Access service-token credentials; the BOOX app imports or enters it before first contact, validates using Access headers, completes `/pair/complete` with Access headers + pair secret + device public key, persists `cloudflareAccessClientId`/`cloudflareAccessClientSecret` per machine, and presents those headers on every public-mode HTTP request and Socket.IO websocket/polling handshake. Blessed BOOX completes a remote session over evyatar.dev with Dev Tunnels off, off-LAN. `/pair/complete` yields key material ONLY in operator window w/ QR secret; replay-protected. Cloudflare Access service-token policy proven to reject missing/incorrect headers and allow WS upgrade only with valid service-token headers. Opt-in/default-off; Dev Tunnels unchanged. All existing tests pass + new generated route-inventory fail-closed/no-leak tests.
